description: Extend the split-mega inner solve to k>448 for the WELL-CONDITIONED reduced blocks of shapes 4 (dense1024 low-rank k=608, 76.9ms) & 10 (nearrank1024 k=768, 107ms) -- brief-26+30 both name this 'the real prize': these two shapes' inner k-by-k Rayleigh eigh is STUCK on cuSOLVER because k>448 overflows the single-CTA packed-FP16-triangle SMEM cap (262KB>228KB at k=512). DISTINCT from the refuted full-n dense-reduction briefs (1/3/4/6/9/14/21): those solved the ILL-CONDITIONED full matrix (or shape-11's FP16-precision-walled flat-to-ulp spectrum) at large batch where cuSOLVER fills 148 SMs. HERE the target is the REDUCED block Bk=Qd^T A Qd -- WELL-CONDITIONED (dominant subspace of a cond~100 matrix, so FP16's 10-bit mantissa resolves it, NO precision wall like shape 11 -- brief-30 confirmed the k-cliff is COST not accuracy for these), at SMALL batch b60 (cuSOLVER fills only ~60 of 148 SMs, so it's MORE beatable than the b640 cases). Two build options: (a) reuse brief-14's WORKING 2-CTA thread-block-cluster infra (compute_100a, cudaLaunchKernelEx, map_shared_rank DSMEM, cg::cluster) to split the packed-FP16 k-triangle across 2 CTAs' DSMEM (k=608 packed=370KB/2=185KB/CTA<228KB; k=768=576KB/2=288KB>228KB so k=768 needs C=3 or tiling); reuse brief-25's mega_latrd_panel_k + the split back-transform; OR (b) tile the FP16 triangle out of SMEM (stream panels). Start with shape 4 (k=608, C=2 fits) as the cleaner target; shape 10 (k=768) only if C=2 generalizes. Route ONLY these reduced blocks via the low-rank inner-solve path; per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback so a slow/inaccurate block falls back (no regression). If the reduced-block cluster solve is STILL slower than cuSOLVER at b60 (measure the kernel vs cuSOLVER-on-the-k608-block-batch), refute cleanly -- that closes the biggest open question. -O3/--use_fast_math (accepted-best flags); no 'stream' substring (use cg::cluster/map_shared_rank, NEVER cudaStream); NVCC-heavy but contention currently clear (siblings pure-torch); forks best a7f01e4d; verify 39/39 twice + quiet re-bench beats 35659.

t1: wire C=2 cluster split kernel (mega_eigh_clust_split, forked brief-14) for k=608 inner solve, routed k in (448,680] via _lr_reduced_clust. DIRECT kernel-vs-cuSOLVER probe on shape-4 k=608 b60 block: cluster inner 21.2ms vs cuSOLVER 48.3ms = 2.28x FASTER kernel, orth 2.7e-3 (GOOD, <5.8e-3 gate) BUT eigr/anorm 1.99 >> 1.09e-2 gate -> 60/60 fail. Block is ILL-conditioned (cond~71457, ~52 near-zero clustered eigs); FP16-tridiag+twisted eigenVECTOR stage fails on the near-degenerate near-zero cluster (eigr huge even w/ Rayleigh-refreshed eigenvalues). REGRESSION: shape4 76874->156084us (outer gate falls all 60 to FULL-n cuSOLVER, 2x), geomean 35454->37563. Speed IS there (2.28x); accuracy is the wall. 39/39 validate PASS (fallback catches).

t2: DE-RACED the cluster tridiag -> shape-4 k=608 WIN. Root cause of t1 NaN/nondeterminism was NOT accuracy (brief premise refuted) but a cross-CTA RACE in the DSMEM map_shared_rank peer reads of reflector v + symv result p (brief-21 hit same, unfixed). FIX: exchange v/p via GLOBAL staging (vgm/pgm) + __threadfence() + cluster.sync; scalar reductions (amax/s2/alpha) stay DSMEM. Attempts that did NOT fix it (for manager): fence-before-cl.sync on pgm scalars, DSMEM clx scalars, volatile peer ptrs, -O2 vs -O3, drop launch_bounds. RESULT on real shape-4 k=608 b60 block: DETERMINISTIC (run-to-run diff 0.0), orth 1.2e-3<5.8e-3 gate, eigr/an 2.1e-3<1.09e-2 gate, nbad 0/60; CLUSTER inner 22.9ms vs cuSOLVER 48.3ms=2.11x. END-TO-END: shape4 76874->51383us (-33%, 1.50x), geomean 35454->34511us (-2.66%, BEATS parent+target 35401). Validated 39/39 TWICE (determinism under --use_fast_math confirmed). nsys: clust_split_k now 41.4% of shape4 (no syevd -> cuSOLVER gone). shape10 k=768 unchanged (C=2 fits 608 not 768=590KB packed). Forked 5c66a54b3.

t3: runtime cluster size C (one build serves C=2 k=608 + C=3 k=768). Made C a runtime kernel arg (removed __cluster_dims__/CLUST_C define, cluster dim via launch attr) + generalized symv peer reads / v-p exchange / scalar reductions over arbitrary C. MEASURED shape-10 k=768 C=3: CORRECT (deterministic, orth 5.2e-3<5.9e-3, eigr/an 9.9e-3<1.09e-2, nbad 0/60 -- de-race generalizes to C=3) BUT cluster inner 83ms vs cuSOLVER 67ms = 0.81x (3-way coordination + 24 tridiag panels @ n=768), routing it REGRESSED shape10 108639->124664us. CAPPED _MEGA_CLUST_KMAX=682 (C=2 only); k=768 stays cuSOLVER. shape-4 C=2 still wins but the C-generic exchange cost ~4ms (shape4 51383->55600, geomean 34511->34770). 39/39 TWICE. Quiet geomean 34718-34784 (beats parent 35454 + target 35401). t4 will restore the tight per-peer exchange.

t4: FUSED single-pass symv -> BOTH shape-4 AND shape-10 beat cuSOLVER. The t3 C-generic split-symv iterated the owned-row loop once per peer rank (~4ms cost). Re-fused into one row-loop pass (lower + local-upper + each peer rank's rows, peer Ah ptrs resolved once). Recovered shape-4 to 22.1ms (cuSOLVER 48.3=2.19x) AND flipped shape-10 C=3 0.81x->1.06x (63.7 vs 67.3ms) -> raised kmax to 836 so k=768 routes. MEASURED quiet (2 runs agree): shape4 76874->50470us (-34%, C=2 k=608), shape10 108639->104968us (-3.4%, C=3 k=768), GEOMEAN 35454->34343us (-3.1%, BEATS parent+target 35401). Per-matrix gate safe: shape10 outer nbad 0/60 across 3 reseeds. 39/39 validated TWICE. nsys: clust_split_k 40.3% of shape4, 57.8% of shape10 (cuSOLVER gone from shape4). Both target shapes off the cuSOLVER floor -- the brief's real prize.

WIN -- delivered the brief's 'real prize': BOTH shapes 4 & 10 moved off the cuSOLVER floor. HEAD=f8e44f9d1 (t4), quiet geomean 35454->34343us (-3.1%, beats parent + target 35401), 39/39 validated TWICE (deterministic under -O3/--use_fast_math). shape4 76874->50466us (-34%), shape10 108639->104886us (-3.5%); all 11 other shapes byte-unchanged (shape3 81030, shape8 93187, shape9 47044, shape12 33876 = parent). No 'stream' substring.

APPROACH: Adapted brief-14's mega_eigh_clust512 into mega_eigh_clust_split -- a SPLIT-output C-CTA thread-block-cluster reduced-block eigensolver: the packed-FP16 k-triangle is row-distributed across C CTAs' DSMEM (k=608 370KB/2=185KB/CTA C=2; k=768 590KB/3=197KB/CTA C=3, both <228KB), tridiag+Sturm+twisted distributed, block-T built on rank 0, then the EXISTING torch tensor-core WY back-transform (_mega_med_backtransform) forms Q. Routed k in (448,836] via _lr_reduced_clust in _lr_reduced_eigh; the OUTER low-rank A@V gate is the per-matrix cuSOLVER fallback (0 fallbacks measured on 4/10). C is a RUNTIME kernel arg so one build serves both.

KEY QUESTION ANSWERED: does a cluster reduced-block solve at k=608 b60 BEAT cuSOLVER? YES -- cluster inner 22.1ms vs cuSOLVER 48.3ms = 2.19x (C=2 k=608); 63.7ms vs 67.3ms = 1.06x (C=3 k=768). Both gate-pass at nbad 0/60 (inner) and outer nbad 0/60 across 3 reseeds.

THE DE-RACE (the crux): t1 wired it and REGRESSED (shape4 156084us) -- brief-14's distributed tridiag produced NON-DETERMINISTIC/NaN tridiagonals (brief-21 hit the same, couldn't fix). Root cause: the DSMEM map_shared_rank PEER READS of the reflector v + symv result p race. FIXED by exchanging v/p through GLOBAL staging (vgm/pgm) + __threadfence() + cluster.sync (scalar reductions amax/s2/alpha stay DSMEM, race-free). Attempts that did NOT fix it (so the manager needn't retry): __threadfence before cl.sync on the pgm scalar writes; DSMEM scalar reductions; volatile peer pointers; -O2 vs -O3; removing __launch_bounds__(nt,2). t4 then FUSED the split C-generic symv back to a single row-loop pass, recovering shape4 to 2.19x AND flipping shape10 C=3 0.81x->1.06x.

TRIAL ARC: t1 wire cluster (racy, shape4 REGRESSED 156084, geomean 37563) -> t2 DE-RACE via global v/p exchange (shape4 51383, geomean 34511, C=2 only) -> t3 runtime-C + C-generic (C=3 k=768 correct but 0.81x, C-generic exchange cost ~4ms, geomean 34767) -> t4 FUSED symv (shape4 50466 2.19x + shape10 C=3 1.06x, geomean 34343, BEST).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not pursued, all would deepen this win):
(1) BLOCKED/PANEL tridiag inside the cluster kernel (brief-25's mega_latrd_panel_k approach): the cluster kernel is 40% of shape4 / 58% of shape10 and is dominated by the SERIAL per-column tridiag with a GLOBAL v/p round-trip EACH of ~600-766 columns. A panel (NB reflectors) tridiag with the trailing two-sided update as a torch tensor-core GEMM would cut the cluster.sync + global-exchange count ~NBx -- the single biggest lever, esp. for shape10 where C=3's win is thin (1.06x). Would let shape10 win by much more, and possibly enable C=3->C=2 for k=768 if the panel shrinks SMEM.
(2) FASTER cross-CTA v/p exchange: the global-staging + __threadfence() exchange is correct but slower than brief-14's (racy) DSMEM. A race-free DSMEM exchange (e.g. a cluster-scoped acquire/release fence pattern, or double-buffered peer SMEM slots) would recover the DSMEM speed the de-race gave up (~1-2ms/call).
(3) shape10 orth margin is THIN (outer orth 9.6e-3 vs 9.77e-3 gate at seed 770005/770025): a cheap Newton-Schulz reorth of the inner eigenvectors (brief-30's _lr_ns_reorth, flag OFF) on the k=768 block would widen the margin, making the C=3 route robust to reseeds AND possibly letting a smaller k route.
(4) shapes 3/8/12 (k=352/384, on the fast single-CTA mega path) could re-sweep k UPWARD now that k>448 has a fast cluster path -- a larger k = smaller complement = cheaper CQR2, if the cluster inner cost at the larger k stays below the complement saving (brief-30 found the single-CTA cost cliff above k~384; the cluster may flatten it).
(5) The cluster kernel's back-transform is torch tensor-core (good) but the block-T build is rank-0-only (other ranks idle in stage 4) -- distributing it could shave the tail.
